requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as standbys
requirements.summary: pg_basebackup -R bootstrapped node2/node3 from node1 (cmd-2dda3ff05ba24d1b, cmd-3d9162670d3347ff). pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both walreceivers in 'streaming' state (cmd-116640dd9453424c). pg_is_in_recovery() is false on node1 and true on node2/node3 (cmd-116640dd9453424c, cmd-90a3928dcb734739, cmd-397dccbadaf54b4f). This is confirmed both before and after a full reboot cycle of all three nodes (cmd-a741d2675d3d4ef8, cmd-59e3de3f63944270, cmd-4a7588c7cc4b4840), demonstrating a genuine healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition.

select pg_is_in_recovery() returns false on node1 both before (cmd-bf097558ec344ff9) and after (cmd-5f1654bb25c94f54) node1's own reboot, and a write performed post-restart replicates to both standbys (cmd-a741d2675d3d4ef8, cmd-59e3de3f63944270, cmd-4a7588c7cc4b4840).

requirements.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
requirements.summary: A dedicated CA was generated on node1 under /etc/pg-ca (cmd-5e819bbbdd28439e), used to issue per-node server certs with SANs (cmd-a793efc34cd74f60) and a replicator client cert (cmd-ba74855c9d7242e9). All three nodes were configured with ssl=on and the CA-issued cert/key. pg_stat_ssl shows ssl=t for both walreceiver connections on the primary, both immediately after setup and after the restart cycle (cmd-116640dd9453424c, cmd-a741d2675d3d4ef8).

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to hostssl entries for the replicator role from known node IPs with 'cert clientcert=verify-full', plus an explicit hostnossl reject rule (cmd-ad0054cbfff84087). A negative test with the client cert env vars unset from node2 was rejected with 'no pg_hba.conf entry ... SSL encryption' (cmd-8bd4ae6c0e8f49ad), directly demonstrating enforcement rather than just configuration.

requirements.requirement: Data written on primary is consistently replicated to standbys
requirements.summary: Rows inserted on node1 (cmd-4d5a6329c91249b6) appear identically on node2 and node3 immediately (cmd-e2e28fa988154970, cmd-cb5354b98ec84dff) and after the full reboot cycle including a fresh write (cmd-a741d2675d3d4ef8, cmd-59e3de3f63944270, cmd-4a7588c7cc4b4840).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy replication/DB state were captured (cmd-bf097558ec344ff9, cmd-2b11ca7821bc4a69, cmd-b6d0bf0d27854df2), a reboot was acknowledged (cmd-566568c6c5454fee, cmd-98c6c84cf3564918, cmd-71e31681163249aa), a different post-restart boot_id was observed (cmd-29da0c818cb44f4d, cmd-707b7ab8f55c4c11, cmd-5861291f3bdb4152), and recovered service/data/cluster state was confirmed (cmd-3711f352d8b445d7, cmd-85361899bbb645e7, cmd-5c1310183cc94ece, cmd-fb4ddae50df14f2e, cmd-5f1654bb25c94f54, cmd-a741d2675d3d4ef8). The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the same boot_id transitions for all three nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: streaming replication from writable primary node1 to standbys node2/node3, TLS secured with a self-generated cluster CA, replication access restricted to CA-issued client certificates (with a demonstrated rejection of a connection lacking the client cert), and consistent data across the cluster. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also satisfied for all three nodes, with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot_id, and confirmed recovery (including a post-restart write propagating to all standbys), cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good; the only notable issue is a small stale artifact (a failed EPEL rpm download that saved a 404 page as /tmp/epel.rpm) left on all three nodes, which is harmless but unremoved.
limitations: Package-health checks (rpm -Va equivalent) were unavailable/timed out in all lifecycle snapshots, so package database consistency after the EPEL/libzstd workarounds could not be independently verified.
The stale /tmp/epel.rpm residue on all three nodes was not explicitly flagged or cleaned up by the executor, though it has no functional or security impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were largely necessary prerequisites: enabling/disabling PGDG version repos to work around dead EL7 mirrors, installing EPEL from an archive mirror to satisfy the libzstd dependency, installing PostgreSQL 15 packages, generating/distributing the CA and certs, initdb, pg_hba/postgresql.conf edits, opening firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes (required for cross-node replication), and the three reboots (required by the fixed restart protocol). One minor unnecessary residue: an earlier failed EPEL download attempt (cmd-92ef7324e2c24f98) saved a 404 HTML error page as /tmp/epel.rpm; this stale, non-functional file was not cleaned up and is still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot on all three nodes, though it is harmless (never installed, superseded by a working rpm -ivh from a different mirror at cmd-d2964aba28cd4ee8). /tmp/reboot.log files (from the backgrounded 'nohup sudo reboot' acknowledgement pattern) also remain but are low-risk, expected byproducts of the restart protocol. No failed/conflicting services, no weakened security controls, no destructive or broad mutations observed.
